notes.RT1 Genre precision: Primary Sci-Fi + Cyberpunk Action Thriller precisely fits neural simulation, pod fields, Agents and wire-fu physics-bending (ev-013 sc-039, ev-003 sc-005).

notes.RT3 Elevator pitch dual test: Logline gives hacker, unkillable Agents, red-pill reveal and rescue to prove One; premise expands with pod extraction and 303 death/revival without invention (ev-011 sc-031, ev-044 sc-209).
notes.RT4 Entity roster coverage: Covers Neo/Trinity/Morpheus/Smith/Cypher/Tank plus Matrix/Phones/Pods/Sentinels but omits Oracle, Zion and Dozer/Apoc/Switch despite plot centrality (ev-023 sc-085).
notes.RT5 Plot identification: Four distinct plots - Awakening, Rescue of Morpheus, Cypher Betrayal, Crew Survival - each with separate want/resistance/cost, no conflation or missing central thread.
notes.RT6 Per-plot description: Each plot states who wants what, what resists, cost and resolution with ev-anchored beats: dojo/jump failures, steak-deal, EMP timing (ev-015 sc-056, ev-020 sc-074, ev-046 sc-219).
notes.RT7 Writing style unnamed-author test: Tech-noir/Hong Kong wire-fu hybrid described via green code rain, liquefying mirrors, frozen-time reveals without naming Wachowskis, testable in scenes (ev-010 sc-030, ev-018 sc-065).
notes.RT8 Dramatic structure: Clear 3-act with five turning points: White Rabbit inciting, red-pill PP1, desert/dojo midpoint, Oracle/trap PP2, 303 death/resurrection climax all ev-dated (ev-004, ev-010, ev-013, ev-023, ev-043).
notes.RT9 Human-experience topics and dilemmas: Three universal dilemmas - truth vs illusion, preservation vs sacrifice, fate vs choice - each with both horns priced and anchored in red/blue pill and re-entry choice (ev-010 sc-028, ev-032 sc-148).
notes.RT10 Protagonist identification value: Admirable truth-seeking vs relatable office-drone numbness (alarm 9:15, Rhineheart lecture, ledge freeze) linked as same splinter with escalating costs to death/revival (ev-005 sc-014, ev-006 sc-017, ev-043 sc-205).
